summary: @servicetitan/carto-rn-kit preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (string-array with _0x-style identifiers) and, at install time, checks for a local bun binary; if absent it downloads a Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a tmpdir, extracts and chmods it, then execFileSync's the downloaded Bun to run a sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line Bun-only file (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using a rotated string-array (WV8StW shift) with a numeric-index decoder (hc1jfK9), so its contents cannot be inspected by Node-based tooling. The advertised purpose is a React Native component kit (README documents only a Button component, peer deps react/react-native, no native addon, no binding.gyp, no C/C++ sources) — nothing in the stated purpose requires Bun or a large obfuscated Bun-only bundle. The dropper is the alternate-runtime-execution pattern: Bun is installed from its official domain, but Bun is then used to execute the package's own shipped obfuscated payload whose behavior cannot be verified from Node-side inspection. Package name is @servicetitan/carto-rn-kit, inconsistent with the shipped preinstall dropper and consistent with a scope-compromise / malicious-publish scenario.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
